title: Your First Top-Down RPG
description: Create a 2D top-down RPG with painted tilemaps, 8-way character movement, 4-direction animations, and interactive world triggers.

blocks.content: In this tutorial, you will build a 2D top-down RPG exploration scene in about **20 minutes**. You will paint a tilemap world, move a character smoothly in eight directions with zero gravity, animate directional walk cycles, and add interactive chests and area triggers.

items.title: Painted Tilemap Level
items.desc: Design floors, paths, and walls using the built-in **Tilemap** brush and bucket tools.

items.title: 8-Way Normalized Motion
items.desc: Move and sprint smoothly without diagonal speed boosts using **Top-Down Controller**.

items.title: Directional Animation
items.desc: Switch up, down, and side walk clips automatically with **Top-Down Animator**.

items.title: Interactive World Objects
items.desc: Open chests and trigger zone events when the player explores the map.

blocks.content: Complete [Quick Start](getting_started/quick_start) first so you are familiar with creating projects and adding components. Import a top-down tileset image and a 4-direction character spritesheet into the **Assets** dock.

rows: Paints grid-aligned terrain tiles for floors, roads, and walls.
Provides zero-gravity sliding collision around walls and obstacles.
Handles 8-directional input, sprint multipliers, and directional sprite clips.
Detects when the player enters a zone or presses **E** near a chest.

blocks.content: Begin by painting your ground terrain on a [Tilemap](components/renderers/tilemap) entity and placing solid colliders around walls or trees.

items: In the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy), create an entity named **WorldGround** on your world layer.
Select **WorldGround**, click **Add Component** in the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector), and choose **Tilemap**.

Assign your tileset image in the **Tilemap** component, set the tile grid size (for example **32 x 32**), and use the **Brush** (**B**) and **Bucket** (**G**) tools in the [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport) to paint grass and stone paths.

Create a second entity named **Walls** above **WorldGround**, attach **Tilemap**, [Physics Body](components/physics_body) (**Static**), and [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider), and add box collider shapes over impassable walls and trees.

blocks.content: Next, configure the player entity with zero gravity and a foot-aligned collider so the character slides cleanly around corners.

items: In the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy), create an entity named **Hero**, set its **Tag** to **player** in the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector) header, and place it on the path.

Attach [Image Renderer](components/renderers/sprite_renderer), [Sprite Animator](components/sprite_animator), [Physics Body](components/physics_body), and [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider) to **Hero**.
In **Physics Body**, set **Body Type** to **Dynamic**, set **Gravity Scale** to **0**, and enable **Fixed Rotation**.
In **Multi-Collider**, resize and offset the box shape so it covers only the lower half (feet) of the character sprite.
In **Sprite Animator**, create six clips named **idle_down**, **idle_up**, **idle_side**, **walk_down**, **walk_up**, and **walk_side**.

blocks.content: Wire **Hero**'s movement graph and add an interactive treasure chest that opens when the player presses **E**.

items: Attach a [Script Controller](components/script_controller) to **Hero** and open its script in the [Graph & Node Concepts](visual_scripting/graph_concepts) editor.

Add [On Tick](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventTick) and connect its execution and **deltaTime** pins to [Top-Down Controller](node_library/helper_tool#node-topDownController) with **Speed** set to **180** and **Sprint Multiplier** set to **1.5**.

Add [Top-Down Animator](node_library/helper_tool#node-topDownAnimator) after **Top-Down Controller**, connect **isMoving**, **isSprinting**, and **facingDirection**, and leave **Use Side Flip** enabled so one side clip covers both left and right movement.
Wire [On Scene Start](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventSceneStart) to [Camera Follow](node_library/game_renderer#node-actionCameraFollow) so the camera tracks **Hero** across the map.

Create a **Chest** entity with **Image Renderer**, **Sprite Animator** (**closed** and **open** clips), **Physics Body** (**Static**), **Multi-Collider** (**Is Sensor** enabled), and **Script Controller**.

In **Chest**'s graph, wire **On Tick** to [Collectable Item](node_library/helper_tool#node-collectableItem) with **Collector Tag** set to **player**, **Pickup Mode** set to **interact_key**, **Interact Key** set to **e**, and **Collect Clip** set to **open**.

blocks.content: Playtest your top-down RPG level in the viewport.

items: Click **Play** in the top bar.
Move around the tilemap using **W**, **A**, **S**, and **D**, and hold **Shift** to sprint.
Walk into a wall to verify that **Hero** slides smoothly along the collider edge without rotating or getting stuck.
Walk up to **Chest** and press **E** to trigger the opening animation, then click **Stop** and press **Ctrl + S** to save.

blocks.message: If your character floats downward on its own, double-check that **Gravity Scale** on **Hero**'s [Physics Body](components/physics_body) is set to **0**.

blocks.content: Download the completed Top-Down RPG **.lupisproject** sample archive to inspect the painted tilemap, directional animations, and interactive objects directly in the editor.

rows: Painted tilemap village, 8-way character controller, 4-direction animations, camera follow, and interactive pickups.

items: Click the download link in the table above to save the **.lupisproject** archive to your computer.
Open the **My Projects** dashboard in Lupis Engine (see [Project & Export](getting_started/project_and_export#manage-projects)).
Drag and drop the downloaded **.lupisproject** file onto the dashboard, or click **Load Project** and select the file.
Click the imported project card to open the editor, then click **Play** in the top bar to explore the RPG scene.
